 Order

********** The Petitioner has filed the above Writ Petition for issuance of a Writ of Mandamus directing the respondents to remit the eligible compensation amount to the Petitioners land acquired by the first respondent for the purpose of formation of Dindigul Town By pass road to distance about from 0/0 to 10/250 kms as per Tamil Nadu Highways Act, 2001 by considering the Petitioners representation, dated 26.09.2024.

2.Heard the learned counsel appearing on either side and perused the materials placed before this Court.
3.The Petitioner is the owner of some of the subject properties and also is a power agent coupled with aboslute interest for the other properties.
The subject properties were acquired by the second respondent for the purpose of formation of Dindigul Bypass Road under the Tamil Nadu Highways Act, 2001.
For the subject lands compensation amount was awarded in Award No.4 of 2023, dated 22.06.2023.

While so, the Petitioner received a https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis memo, dated 21.12.2023 from the third respondent calling upon him to submit the relevant documents of the subject lands from the year 1960, for the purpose of considering his request seeking compensation for the properties.
On 26.09.2024, the Petitioner submitted a representation along with all the relevant documents as requested by the third respondent for disbursement of compensation for his lands.
As the said representation was not considered, the Petitioner filed the above Writ Petition for the aforesaid relief.
4.Heard both side counsels.
Perused the records.
By consent of the counsels, the Writ Petition is taken up for final disposal.
5.The learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that pending Writ Petition, the third respondent passed an order on 04.12.2024, rejecting the Petitioners claim for disbursement of compensation.

The learned counsel therefore prayed that he may be permitted to challenge the order of the third respondent, dated 04.12.2024.
6.In view of the fact that the Petitioners claim for compensation was rejected by the third respondent on 04.12.2024
, the prayer sought for in the Writ Petition cannot be entertained.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
However, the Petitioner is permtited to challenge the order, dated 4.12.2024 passed by the third respondent in a manner known to law, if so advised.
7.The Writ Petition is disposed of accordingly.
No costs.
